chunks: And this report has been narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Amr ibn Hafsh, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), like it.

The obligatory Hajj is once, and whatever is added to it is recommended and preferred, and there is no disagreement among Muslims regarding this, therefore for that reason we did not occupy ourselves with citing the hadiths regarding it, and that which was narrated is:
ai.seo_question: Is the obligatory Hajj performed only once or multiple times in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), transmitted via the chain of Amr ibn Hafs, confirms the consensus (ijma') among Muslims that the obligatory Hajj is a one-time duty, rendering additional pilgrimages merely recommended (mustahabb). Shaykh al-Tusi omits further evidences for this specific ruling due to its universally accepted status, highlighting the practical scholarly approach of focusing on disputed matters in his work *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*.
